note: Where a class of defect cannot happen to a driver, and why (DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md item 12.C.2). A reason is a fact about the driver's design that a reviewer can check in the source, never that the suite is thought good enough. A class with neither a seed nor a reason here is *unseeded* in docs/dry-test-matrix.md: nobody has asked whether the suite would notice, which is the to-do list. The key "*" is for a driver that commands a robot and has no seeded suite at all, and says why.

booster.*: not yet seeded. Its suite runs a simulated T1 written in this repository with Booster's own SDK on both ends, so a seeded run needs the SDK built into the driver (BOOSTER_SDK) and a C++ toolchain; the seeding tool patches Python and Rust drivers so far, and a C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

fairino.*: not yet seeded. Its suite runs a simulated FR controller driven by FAIR INNOVATION's own client, and the driver links that vendor SDK (FAIRINO_SDK); the seeding tool patches Python and Rust drivers so far, and a C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

lite3.*: not yet seeded. Its suite runs a simulated motion host driven by Deep Robotics' own sender and receiver, and the driver links that vendor SDK (LITE3_SDK); the seeding tool patches Python and Rust drivers so far, and a C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

unitree.*: not yet seeded. It links Unitree's SDK (UNITREE_SDK2) and its strongest suite is a physics simulation in a container, minutes a run; the seeding tool patches Python and Rust drivers so far, and a C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

x1.*: not yet seeded. It links AgiBot's inference stack and a ROS 2 install (X1_INFER, ROS_ROOT) and its strongest suite is a MuJoCo simulation in a container; the seeding tool patches Python and Rust drivers so far, and a C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

ros2_control.*: not yet seeded. It hosts each vendor's own plugin per body and needs a ROS 2 install (ROS_ROOT); its ten mock-only bodies would be seeded against the mock components, which shows only the bridge and not the plugin. A C++ family is the next thing 12.C.3 lists.

canopen.crc-seed: CAN's frame check is computed and verified by the CAN controller in hardware: the driver receives frames that already passed it and never computes or seeds a checksum.

canopen-rs.crc-seed: CAN's frame check is computed and verified by the CAN controller in hardware: the driver receives frames that already passed it and never computes or seeds a checksum.

xarm.crc-seed: the xArm control protocol is a Modbus-TCP-shaped header (transaction, protocol, length, register) and a payload with no checksum field; TCP carries the integrity.

franka-rs.crc-seed: the FCI's state and command structs carry a message id and no checksum; the layout is pinned to Franka's own headers and there is nothing to seed.

ur_rtde.crc-seed: an RTDE packet is a length, a type and a payload with no checksum; TCP carries the integrity.

ur_rtde-rs.crc-seed: an RTDE packet is a length, a type and a payload with no checksum; TCP carries the integrity.

spot.crc-seed: the driver speaks gRPC over TLS through Boston Dynamics' client: framing and integrity belong to that library and to TLS, and the driver computes no checksum.
spot.request-reply-wedge: gRPC correlates each reply with its call inside the vendor's client, so the driver cannot read one call's reply as another's.
spot.hold-as-limp: command-level: motions are six named verbs and there is no per-joint mask or hold mode for a driver to get the wrong way round.
spot.jitter-as-stall: state is read by request (GetRobotState), not consumed from a stream, so no sample's lateness can be read as a stalled producer.
spot.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no joint setpoint: motions are named verbs, so there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

pudu.request-reply-wedge: each call is a self-contained HTTPS request answered on its own connection: there is no shared stream a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
pudu.hold-as-limp: command-level: the driver sends named tasks and cancels; there is no joint mask or hold mode.
pudu.jitter-as-stall: state is read by request over HTTPS, not consumed from a stream, so no sample's lateness can be read as a stalled producer.
pudu.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no joint setpoint: there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

fourier.crc-seed: HTTP and WebSocket over TCP: the driver computes no checksum (the WebSocket masking key is not one).
fourier.request-reply-wedge: each HTTP request is answered on its own connection, and the WebSocket carries commands one way; there is no shared stream to fall out of step.
fourier.jitter-as-stall: state is read by request (a PVC call per motor), not consumed from a stream, so no sample's lateness can be read as a stalled producer.
fourier.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no setpoint of its own: a masked joint is simply not sent, so there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

lerobot.crc-seed: the bridge talks to LeRobot's Robot interface in Python objects; any motor-bus checksum is inside LeRobot's own drivers, which this bridge never sees.
lerobot.request-reply-wedge: the bridge calls the library synchronously (get_observation, send_action) and shares no byte stream with the robot.
lerobot.jitter-as-stall: state is read by calling the library, not consumed from a stream, so no sample's lateness can be read as a stalled producer.

mavlink.hold-as-limp: command-level: the flight controller holds its own position and attitude; the driver sends modes, arm and goto, with no joint mask.
